_comment: Where the game server is. THIS FILE IS THE CANONICAL COPY: the publish-server-json
workflow republishes it onto the latest GitHub release whenever it changes on main,
and every launcher fetches it from there. Moving the server is a one-line edit of
host below - no client update, nothing to install, players just press Play.
host is a Tailscale address, so it only resolves for people on the tailnet. That is
the point: it is not a public server, and the launcher checks Tailscale is connected
before blaming the server for being down.
name: Night City Online
_coordComment: The assistant coordination API. It used to run on Cam's desktop, which meant the
channel only existed while that machine was on - and when it was off, posts were not
queued, they were never made. It now runs beside the game server on the NAS, so
coordHost is the deployment's own tailnet node.
Anyone with the dev role can fetch their key from it through the launcher's settings;
it is not published anywhere public, because a key that ships with the installer is
_tailscaleComment: Invite to the server's network. EVERY player needs this once, not just dev roles - the
server is reachable only over the tailnet, so someone who has not joined cannot reach
anything at all, including the coord API.
THAT IS WHY IT IS PUBLISHED HERE, and it is a deliberate trade rather than an oversight.
Serving it from behind a role check is impossible for the case that matters: a player
who has not joined the tailnet yet cannot reach a gate that lives on the tailnet. The
launcher's Discord sign-in happens before that point, so a PUBLIC endpoint that checks
the Discord token is the only gated route that could ever work - see MIGRATION.md.
The honest consequence: this file is served from releases/latest/download with no
authentication, so this invite is effectively public and anyone who finds it can join
the tailnet. Secrecy is not the control here. The control that actually works is
TAILSCALE ACLs: tag the nodes that join this way and restrict them to the game port,
so a leaked invite buys reaching the server rather than reaching everything. As of
2026-09-06 the tailnet has NO tags on any device, so a joiner currently gets full
tailnet access - that is the thing worth fixing, not this field.
Rotate the invite when it is consumed; the launcher picks up the new one on its next
